title: 新竹
author: 郑燮
intro: A painter famous for bamboo looks at this year’s new shoots, already taller than the old stalks — and sees a lesson about the young and the old helping each other.
analysis: 郑板桥一生爱画竹、写竹。这首诗写新竹：新长出来的竹子比老竹子还高，但它能长这么高，全靠老竹的枝干扶持。后两句往前看：明年还会有新竹长出来，长到十丈高，绕满整个池塘。“龙孙”是竹笋、新竹的美称，“凤池”是池塘的美称，一龙一凤，显得新竹生机勃勃。表面写竹，其实写人：年轻一代超过老一辈，是因为老一辈的扶持；而一代又一代传下去，事业才越来越兴旺。这种借写景物来讲道理的写法叫“托物言志”。诗的语言很浅，适合初学者读，也常被老师用来说师生、父子之间的关系。
analysisEn: Zheng Banqiao spent his life painting and writing about bamboo. Here he notices that the new bamboo has grown taller than the old — yet it could only grow so tall because the old stalks held it up. Then he looks ahead: next year more shoots will come, rising ten zhang high (over thirty metres, a deliberate exaggeration) and circling the whole pond. “Dragon grandchildren” is a fond name for bamboo shoots and “phoenix pool” a fine name for a pond, so the poem ends with dragons and phoenixes — full of life. On the surface it is about plants; underneath it is about people. The young surpass the old because the old support them, and each generation passes things on to the next. Saying something about life through an object like this is called tuō wù yán zhì, “using a thing to express an idea”. The words are simple, which makes it a good poem for beginners, and teachers often quote it when talking about students and teachers, or children and parents.
background: Zheng Xie (1693–1765), better known as Zheng Banqiao, was a Qing official, calligrapher and painter, one of the “Eight Eccentrics of Yangzhou”. Bamboo, orchids and rocks were his favourite subjects, and many of his poems were written on his own paintings.
pronunciation: 干：老干 lǎo gàn（树干的“干”，不读 gān）。为：为扶持 wéi（作为、成为之义，口语也有读 wèi 的）。机器朗读已替换。
version: 采用通行文本。维基文库所据本第三句作“下年再有新生者”，网站从通行本作“明年”。郑燮生卒年一般作 1693–1765（或 1766）。

lines.py: xīn zhú gāo yú jiù zhú zhī
lines.lit: New bamboo is taller than the old bamboo’s stalks,
lines.en: The new bamboo stands taller than the old,

lines.py: quán píng lǎo gàn wéi fú chí
lines.lit: relying entirely on the old trunks as support.
lines.en: but only because the old stems held it up.

lines.py: míng nián zài yǒu xīn shēng zhě
lines.lit: Next year there will again be newly born ones,
lines.en: Next year, when new shoots rise again,

lines.py: shí zhàng lóng sūn rào fèng chí
lines.lit: ten-zhang dragon grandchildren circling the phoenix pool.
lines.en: a forest of young dragons will ring the pool.

words.note: “高于”就是“比……高”，现代书面语仍用。
现代汉语也说“全凭”“全靠”。
现代汉语常用，如“互相扶持”。
现代还说“一落千丈”“万丈高楼”。
原指宫中池沼，这里是池塘的美称。

imagery.name: 竹
imagery.zh: 新竹和老竹代表年轻一代和老一辈：新的超越旧的，靠的是旧的扶持。
imagery.en: New and old bamboo stand for the young and the old generation — the new surpass the old with the old’s support.

imagery.name: 水
imagery.zh: “凤池”是竹林环绕的池塘，新竹将来会长满池边，一片兴旺。
imagery.en: The “phoenix pool” will one day be ringed with new bamboo — a picture of flourishing growth.
